proj-1.title: Week 1 · Day 1 — Walk the graph
proj-1.bodyHtml:
Monday, Sep 14 · Week 1, day 1 of 5 · B + C double, ~110 min · Phase 1 · Read the track · Describing motion

Today's targets

SlugI can…Puedo…Type
pp.w01.sketch-firstI can sketch the graph of a motion before the screen shows it, and fix my sketch from the evidence.Puedo dibujar la gráfica de un movimiento antes de que la pantalla la muestre, y corregir mi dibujo con la evidencia.Reasoning
pp.w01.read-graphI can read a position–time or velocity–time graph and say in words how the object moved.Puedo leer una gráfica de posición–tiempo o velocidad–tiempo y decir con palabras cómo se movió el objeto.Knowledge

Language objective (Speaking). Level 1: Answer "faster / slower / stopped?" about a graph. Level 3+: Describe a graph's motion in two sentences. Digo si va más rápido, más lento o parado. Posted, read aloud, tracked met / not yet — never in the physics grade.

Before they walk in

Open Walk the graph / Camina la gráfica from this lesson’s teaching tool. Keep the class controls available. The three tabs map to w01d1-predict, w01d1-talk, and w01d1-write. Use the block picker to project the score table or the individual exit when needed.

  • Project the Walk tab with blank axes. Ask students to name time and position and give units before pressing “Label the axes.” Position means metres from the detector; this is not cumulative distance travelled.
  • Each student opens the lesson to save evidence. Practice notes in the tool are temporary. Keep one detector per group, Logger Lite / Graphical Analysis, and floor tape at 1, 2, and 3 m for physical walks. The on-screen walker is a simulation; it does not read a connected detector.
  • Drag the walker or focus its slider and hold the arrow keys; Shift moves faster. Record automatically focuses the slider for manual walks. Use the lesson tabs or classroom controls to change stages.
  • Post the bilingual word wall and the speaking objective. Keep the Spanish phrase cards below in view.

The 110-minute lesson — hands, record, talk, write

TimeTeach with the toolStudent evidence
0–25 · HANDS / MANOSWalk toward the detector slowly, away faster, then stop. In Free walk, press Record and move the walker for the full 10 s. Compare the same straight floor with falling, rising, and flat lines. Reset between examples. Give every student a physical walk or a turn controlling the simulation. Ask “¿Hacia o lejos?” and “¿Más rápido o más lento?”Oral claims and labeled axes prepare students for w01d1-predict.
25–35 · PREDICT / PREDICESelect Scripted walk · Predict first. Keep the graph covered: start 1 m away, walk away slowly for 3 s, stop for 2 s, and return fast. Students save the first sketch before the teacher selects the reveal. The 10-second scripted run then starts: 1→2.5 m from 0–3 s; stationary 3–5 s; return to 1 m from 5–6 s; stationary to 10 s. Use this timing to interpret the measured trace after the prediction.Save w01d1-predict. Keep the first prediction; explain revisions later rather than replacing it with a copy of the screen.
35–50 · MATCH / COMPARAComplete Match 1 (away, stop), Match 2 (stand, toward fast), and Match 3 (away, stop, back). Selecting a match places the walker at its starting position. Press Record, follow the dashed target for all 10 s, then keep the practice score. Retry and name the change in direction, stopping time, or speed. Partial recordings have no score. A score measures closeness to the target, not mastery.Use the block picker for w01d1-scores. Save each graph number, completed-run score, and one specific fix in the three-row table. Discuss which segment was hardest.
50–75 · TALK / HABLAOpen Talk. Show the prediction and recorded trace. Where do they disagree, and what does the trace support? Start the 60-second timer for speaker A; use Swap for B. Pause/resume as needed. The timer pauses when leaving this tab. Bridge students translate the physics; each learner makes a claim in either language.Rehearse using w01d1-talk: “My sketch goes ___. The trace goes ___. The trace supports ___ because ___.”
75–100 · WRITE / ESCRIBEOpen Write. Level 1 selects bilingual words; Level 2 completes a frame with because; Level 3 explains a chosen segment in their own words. Compare steeper and less-steep lines on the same axis scales. Up means away, flat means stopped, and greater slope magnitude means faster.Save the explanation in w01d1-write. The projected tool rehearses the response; the lesson saves it.
100–110 · CLOSE / CIERREProject the individual exit from the block picker. Ask for direction, stopped/moving, slope evidence, and comparison with the first prediction. Then self-rate 1–3. Tomorrow: use simulations to check a graph already sketched.audit-evidence-exit, then w01d1-rate.

Say it in Spanish

SayMeansWhen
Miren.Watch.Before your own first walk, and before each new graph. Point at the screen, not at yourself.
Primero esto.This first.Handing over the detector — one step, one gesture.
¿Más rápido o más lento?Faster or slower?The either/or check after every walk. This is the day's Level 1 speaking objective — the answer is one word.
Dibuja.Draw.Starting the RECORD segment. Say it, then point at the sketch pad.
Muéstrame.Show me.When you cannot tell whether a student understood. Never ask why in the hands segment.
En español está bien.In Spanish is fine.The first time a Level 1 student stalls on the write. Say it before they ask.
Bien. Eso es física.Good. That is physics.When a labeled sketch is right and the sentence is not. This is the fairness rule said out loud.

Read them off the card. Pronunciation does not matter; using them does. Never ask a Level 1 student a why question in the hands segment.

Formative checks — the walk-around

  • Sketch before the screen — walk the room during the hands segment and look for a pencil moving before a laptop does. A student who only ever draws after the trace appears has not met sketch-first no matter how good the copy is.
  • On the sketch: is toward / away / stopped labeled at all? Labels in Spanish count. An unlabeled correct-looking curve is weaker evidence than a labeled rough one.
  • In the match-score table: does the third column say what they fixed, or just repeat the score? The fix is the learning — an empty fix column is the block to reopen.
  • Language objective (Speaking, Level 1): can the student answer faster / slower / stopped? about a trace without the bridge answering for them? Mark met / not yet by name on the walk-around. Never in the physics score.

The misconception to press

The graph is a picture of the path.

A rising position–time line gets read as walking uphill, or as walking to the right; a V-shaped trace gets read as “they went down and came back up.” It is the single most durable wrong idea in kinematics and it will quietly wreck the ramp week if it survives.

The move: Stop the room the first time you hear it. Walk in a dead straight line toward the detector — the line falls. Same straight line, same floor, walk away — it rises. Ask: “The floor did not change. What changed?” Then the either/or in Spanish: ¿Hacia o lejos? Let a bridge carry the sentence. Do not lecture it; walk it twice.

Lesson and teaching-tool alignment

Source: Motion graphs for SEI physics · Walk the graph. Lesson pp-w01-d1, plan day 11, Week 1 Day 1. The lesson’s existing capture IDs and targets remain the evidence source; the tool’s score and writing controls are temporary practice. All work is saved through the lesson, and only the teacher rates physics mastery.

Confirm the first prediction is saved before revealing the script. Look for a specific fix in all three match rows. Assess the physics evidence in either language, then collect the individual exit before the self-rating.

proj-1.title: Week 1 · Day 3 — A number out of a graph · slope and area
proj-1.bodyHtml:
Wednesday, Sep 16 · Week 1, day 3 of 5 · B + C double, ~110 min · Phase 1 · Read the track · Describing motion

Today's targets

SlugI can…Puedo…Type
pp.w01.v-from-slopeI can find velocity from the slope of a position–time graph.Puedo hallar la velocidad a partir de la pendiente de una gráfica posición–tiempo.Skill
pp.w01.areaI can find displacement from the area under a velocity–time graph.Puedo hallar el desplazamiento a partir del área bajo una gráfica velocidad–tiempo.Skill

Language objective (Speaking). Level 1: Answer "faster / slower / stopped?" about a graph. Level 3+: Describe a graph's motion in two sentences. Digo si va más rápido, más lento o parado. Posted, read aloud, tracked met / not yet — never in the physics grade.

Before they walk in

WhereWhat is there
Loaded before the blockMotion graphs teaching tool · Week 1 Day 3, opened from the lesson’s Present controls. Five tabs: Slope → GEWA 1 → Area → GEWA 2 → Talk & Write. Students save their work in the app; checks in the tool are practice. The two sim-library blocks remain available for individual exploration.
On each tableA meter stick and a stopwatch. Not for a lab — for the demonstration that Δx and Δt are two measurements, not two letters.
On the boardThe two moves, drawn not written: an x–t line with a triangle under it, and a v–t rectangle shaded. No formula yet.
PrintedGEWA solve-box slips for anyone who wants to work on paper before typing. The app's GEWA blocks accept the same work.

The block — four segments, hands first

TimeSegmentWhat happensIn the appBloom'sHattie
0–25HANDSTwo measurements, in the room, with the meter stick and the stopwatch: someone walks from a tape mark to another, two people call the distance and the time. Write both on the board. That pair of numbers is the slope, before any graph is mentioned. Then use the teaching tool’s Slope tab: drag both points, show rise and run, and use Two lines to compare a high shallow line with a low steep line.w01d3 (day callout) · w01d3-sim1Understand / ApplyWorked examples · d=0.57
25–50RECORDUse the tool’s GEWA 1 tab to model the equation choice. Students save their own Given, Equation, Work and Answer in w01d3-gewa1. A cart at 2.0 m at t = 1.0 s and 3.0 m at t = 5.0 s — velocity from the slope. The numbers are chosen so the graph ends high and is shallow: v = 0.25 m/s, while the wrong move gives 0.60. Given, equation, work, answer. The equation picker offers four; choosing the wrong one is diagnostic, not fatal.w01d3-gewa1 (target: v-from-slope)ApplyWorked examples · d=0.57
50–75RECORD / HANDSUse the tool’s Area tab, shade the rectangle, then choose GEWA 2: 0.40 m/s for 6.0 s, displacement from the area. Say the sentence that makes it obvious — signed area under velocity–time gives displacement; for this forward-only motion, distance equals displacement — while shading the rectangle with your finger on the screen.w01d3-sim2 · w01d3-gewa2 (target: area)ApplyFeedback · d=0.70
75–100TALK, then WRITEUse Talk & Write. Pairs: which move gives a velocity and which gives a distance — and why does that make sense? Then the frame: the slope of x–t tells me ___; the area under v–t tells me ___.w01d3-talk · w01d3-writeAnalyze / UnderstandClassroom discussion · d=0.82
100–110CLOSESave the individual graph exit (audit-evidence-exit) and self-rating (w01d3-rate) in the lesson. Tell them tomorrow is a real cart and they will draw its graph before it moves.——Metacognitive strategies · d=0.60

Say it in Spanish

SayMeansWhen
Primero esto.This first.Given, then equation, then work — one step at a time, with a finger on each box.
Escribe el número.Write the number.Every GEWA box. A number in the right box is evidence even with no sentence around it.
Muéstrame.Show me.Point at the two dots on the screen instead of asking for the words “rise over run.”
¿Más grande o más pequeño?Bigger or smaller?Comparing two slopes. The either/or is the Level 1 route into a comparison.
En español está bien.In Spanish is fine.The write segment. Say it before anyone stalls.

Read them off the card. Pronunciation does not matter; using them does. Never ask a Level 1 student a why question in the hands segment.

Formative checks — the walk-around

  • In GEWA 1, look at the equation step, not the answer. A student who uses the last position divided by the last time and gets 0.60 m/s has not yet used the two graph readings; a student who picks v = Δx/Δt and fumbles the subtraction has the target and needs two minutes.
  • The subtraction is where this day is actually lost: 3.0 − 2.0 over 5.0 − 1.0, so v = 0.25 m/s. The wrong move — last position over last time — gives 3.0/5.0 = 0.60 m/s, nearly two and a half times bigger, so it is visible on the walk-around. Any answer near 0.6 is the misconception below arriving as arithmetic.
  • On the write: does area get attached to a distance, or is it still a word about shapes? For this forward-only example, “The area tells me how far” is useful evidence; ask for the readings, units and reasoning before rating the target.
  • Language objective (Speaking, Level 1): answers bigger / smaller about two slopes. Met / not yet.

The misconception to press

Slope is how high the line is.

Students read the y-value where the line ends instead of its steepness — so a line that ends high “has a big velocity” even when it is nearly flat. It survives because on many textbook graphs the two happen to agree. It will not agree on the ramp.

The move: Draw two lines on the same axes: one starting at 0 and climbing steeply to 2 m in 2 s, one starting at 3 m and creeping to 3.5 m in the same 2 s. Ask which is faster. The high one is slower and looks bigger, and the room will split — that split is the lesson. Then hand it to the pairs with the press: “Which number on the graph did you use, and where is the other one?” Make them point at both the rise and the run before anyone says an answer. The GEWA above is built to the same shape, so the number in the box is the check — 0.25 with the two-reading calculation supports the target; 0.60 flags last-position/last-time reasoning.

proj-1.title: Week 1 · Day 5 — The reasoning artifact
proj-1.bodyHtml:
Friday, Sep 18 · Week 1, day 5 of 5 · B + C double, ~110 min · Phase 1 · Read the track · Describing motion

Today's targets

SlugI can…Puedo…Type
pp.w01.read-graphI can read a position–time or velocity–time graph and say in words how the object moved.Puedo leer una gráfica de posición–tiempo o velocidad–tiempo y decir con palabras cómo se movió el objeto.Knowledge
pp.w01.sketch-firstI can sketch the graph of a motion before the screen shows it, and fix my sketch from the evidence.Puedo dibujar la gráfica de un movimiento antes de que la pantalla la muestre, y corregir mi dibujo con la evidencia.Reasoning

Language objective (Speaking). Level 1: Answer "faster / slower / stopped?" about a graph. Level 3+: Describe a graph's motion in two sentences. Digo si va más rápido, más lento o parado. Posted, read aloud, tracked met / not yet — never in the physics grade.

Before they walk in

WhereWhat is there
Before the blockRecord 07 (/images/sei/mystery-xt.svg) rendered large on the projector and on every device. Check it reads at the back of the room — the diagram is the sentence a Level 1 student can read.
On each tableBlank grid paper for artifact 2, even though the sketch block accepts drawing. Two passes — pencil, then the app — is the SEI move, not a redundancy.
In the appOpen the Lobby launcher: w01d5-artifact is lobby-ready, and the grouping should spread the WIDA bands. Same-day rule — the self-rating holds until each student's own exit ticket is in.
On the wallThe week's five targets as icons with 1–2–3 circles beside them, for the paper rating strip before the screen one.

The block — four segments, hands first

TimeSegmentWhat happensIn the appBloom'sHattie
0–25HANDS (on paper)No new equipment. Record 07 goes up with no explanation and one instruction: label the four segments A–D on your own copy, in either language. Silence for the first five minutes. A Level 1 student who labels A–D correctly has already produced physics evidence.w01d5 (day callout) · w01d5-fig (figure, full width)UnderstandPrior achievement · d=0.41
25–55WRITE (artifact 1)Describe the motion segment by segment, then defend one segment: which feature of the graph proves the description, and the velocity as a number. This is the graded evidence of the week — protect the time.w01d5-artifact (observation, lobby-ready, tiered frames)Analyze / EvaluateFeedback · d=0.70
55–75TALK (lobby)Launch the lobby on the artifact block with mixed-band groups. Debrief on one thing only: a claim someone could prove wrong from the graph. Close the session — role XP lands, and the discourse role is logged with the response.Lobby launcher → w01d5-artifact · w01d5-talkEvaluateClassroom discussion · d=0.82
75–100WRITE (artifact 2)The reverse move: draw the graph that would match a motion given in words — still 2 m away for 2 s, away steadily for 4 s, back faster than it left. Then the exit ticket.w01d5-draw (sketch) · w01-exitCreateElaboration · d=0.60
100–110RATEPaper strip first, screen second. Five targets, 1–2–3. The rating opens only after their own exit ticket — that is the app enforcing MC-6, not a glitch. Issue the off-week question out loud and in writing: watch one thing move for ten seconds and sketch its v–t graph from memory.w01-rate (self-assessment across 5 targets)EvaluateSelf-reported grades · d=1.33

Say it in Spanish

SayMeansWhen
Miren.Watch.Putting Record 07 up. Then say nothing for five minutes.
Etiqueta.Label.The only instruction the first segment needs.
En español está bien.In Spanish is fine.Before the artifact, not during it. Say it to the room, not to a student.
Explícale a tu compañero.Explain it to your partner.Opening the lobby. The oral defense in Spanish is full evidence.
Señala la evidencia.Point to the evidence.When a claim arrives with no graph feature behind it. Pointing is a complete answer at Level 1.
Bien. Eso es física.Good. That is physics.On any labeled-diagram artifact. Say it where the room hears it.

Read them off the card. Pronunciation does not matter; using them does. Never ask a Level 1 student a why question in the hands segment.

Formative checks — the walk-around

  • Walk the artifact as a Level 1 student before you rate anyone: diagram, labels, a number, a frame, an oral defense in Spanish — can that combination reach a 3 on every target this week? If not, the task is wrong, not the student (SEI non-negotiable 11).
  • The defended segment is where reasoning lives. Look for a named graph feature — slope, flat, steepness — attached to a claim. “It moved away” with no feature is a description, not a defense.
  • Artifact 2 catches the students who can read but not produce. A correct description on artifact 1 with a blank or reversed graph on artifact 2 is the profile to name in the cockpit.
  • Calibration: compare each student's self-rating to their artifact evidence. Over-rating is not dishonesty here, it is usually the graph-as-picture idea still running quietly. That is your Week 2 opener.
  • Language objective (Speaking, Level 1): gives the defense in Spanish with the bridge transcribing. Met / not yet, by name — to the ELL team, never in the grade.

The misconception to press

Describing the graph instead of the motion.

“It goes up, then it is flat, then it goes down” is a description of ink. It reads as an answer, it earns nothing on the target, and it is the most common way a whole class quietly fails a reasoning artifact while looking busy.

The move: Ban four words for one round. Tell the room: say what the object did without using up, down, flat or line. It is uncomfortable for about ninety seconds and then the physics vocabulary arrives because nothing else is left — away, toward, steady, faster, stopped. Put the banned words on the board with a line through them and the word bank next to it. For a Level 1 student the ban is easier, not harder: the word bank already holds the words that survive.

Current lesson evidence and projection

Use the class session’s linked target and exit screens. The current learner task and the projector read the same blocks; self-rating uses 1–3 after the individual exit.

  • Work · w01d5-artifact: ARTIFACT 1 · Describe the motion in Record 07, segment by segment (A, B, C, D): which way, how fast, stopped?
  • Work · w01d5-draw: ARTIFACT 2 · Draw the position–time graph that WOULD match: "It sat still 2 m away for 2 s, moved away at a steady speed for 4 s, then came back faster than it left." · ARTEFACTO 2 · Dibuja la gráfica posición–tiempo que correspondería a: «Se quedó quieto a 2 m durante 2 s, se alejó a rapidez constante 4 s, luego regresó más rápido de lo que se fue».
  • Work · w01-exit: EXIT · Week 1 · One thing about graphs that still confuses me — and one thing I can now do that I could not on Monday.
  • Work · w01d5-rate: self_assessment

Check the reasoning and evidence, not completion alone. Optional practice remains available on the learner’s device and in the projector block picker. Preserve the first saved prediction; revisions belong in the later evidence task.
